name: @secforge/chrome-devtools-mcp

tools.name: clear_cookies
tools.description: Deletes cookies from the browser. Pass 'name' and/or 'domain' to delete matching cookies, or 'all' to clear every cookie in the browser. Use this to return to a signed-out or first-visit state.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

domain.description: Only delete cookies for this domain and its subdomains, e.g. "example.com" also matches "www.example.com" but not "notexample.com" (case-insensitive).

name.description: Only delete cookies with this exact name.

all.description: Set to true to delete EVERY cookie in the browser. This signs the user out of every site, so it is required when no other filter is given, to make a full wipe explicit.

tools.name: click
tools.description: Clicks on the provided element

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

uid.description: The uid of an element on the page from the page content snapshot

dblClick.description: Set to true for double clicks. Default is false.

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

tools.name: close_browser
tools.description: Close the whole browser (not a single tab). The browser window is terminated. reconnect_browser can bring it back if a start command or launch configuration is available.

tools.name: close_page
tools.description: Closes the page by its index. The last open page cannot be closed.

pageId.description: The ID of the page to close. Call list_pages to list pages.

tools.name: drag
tools.description: Drag an element onto another element

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

from_uid.description: The uid of the element to drag

to_uid.description: The uid of the element to drop into

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

tools.name: emulate
tools.description: Emulates various features on the target page.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

networkConditions.description: Throttle network. Omit to disable throttling.

cpuThrottlingRate.description: Represents the CPU slowdown factor. Omit or set the rate to 1 to disable throttling

geolocation.description: Geolocation (`<latitude>,<longitude>`) to emulate. Latitude between -90 and 90. Longitude between -180 and 180. Omit to clear the geolocation override.

userAgent.description: User agent to emulate. Set to empty string to clear the user agent override.

colorScheme.description: Emulate the dark or the light mode. Set to "auto" to reset to the default.

viewport.description: Emulate device viewports '<width>x<height>x<devicePixelRatio>[,mobile][,touch][,landscape]'. 'touch' and 'mobile' to emulate mobile devices. 'landscape' to emulate landscape mode.

extraHttpHeaders.description: Extra HTTP headers as a JSON string object, e.g. {"X-Custom": "value", "Authorization": "Bearer token"}. Headers are included into every HTTP request originating from the page and persist across navigations until cleared. Pass an empty string to clear all extra headers.

tools.name: evaluate_script
tools.description: Evaluate JavaScript inside the target page. The source can be provided inline or loaded from a local file. Returns the response as JSON, so returned values have to be JSON-serializable.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

function.description:
JavaScript source to execute in the target page. Provide either this or sourcePath, but not both. The source is interpreted according to format.
Example without arguments: `() => document.title` or `async () => await fetch("example.com")`.
Example with arguments: `(el) => el.innerText`
May contain `{{secret:NAME}}`, which is replaced with the contents of ~/.local/share/chrome-devtools-mcp/secrets/NAME by this MCP server just before the input is sent to the browser, so the secret never has to be passed to this tool. Stage such files by reference (e.g. `pass show x > ~/.local/share/chrome-devtools-mcp/secrets/x`), never by writing the literal value. The secret file is DELETED once the call succeeds; append `:keep` (`{{secret:NAME:keep}}`) to keep it for later calls. Append `:raw` (`{{secret:NAME:raw}}`, `{{secret:NAME:raw:keep}}`) to keep a trailing newline. The directory can be relocated with the CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_SECRETS_DIR environment variable. ALWAYS pick a unique, specific NAME (e.g. "github-login-7f3a" rather than "pw"): ~/.local/share/chrome-devtools-mcp/secrets is shared by all MCP servers running in parallel, so a generic name can be overwritten by another session and make you fill the wrong value, or be deleted while you still need it.
A file given as 'sourcePath' may contain the same placeholders; they are resolved after the file is read.

sourcePath.description: The absolute or relative path to a JavaScript file on the MCP server's local filesystem. Provide either this or function, but not both.

format.description: How to interpret the source. "function" treats it as a function declaration and supports args. "script" evaluates it as classic JavaScript and does not support args. Defaults to "function". ECMAScript modules are not supported.

args.description: An optional list of arguments to pass to the function.

items.description: The uid of an element on the page from the page content snapshot

filePath.description: The absolute or relative path to a file to save the script output to. If omitted, the output is returned inline.

dialogAction.description: Handle dialogs while execution. "accept", "dismiss", or string for response of window.prompt. Defaults to accept.

waitForStableDom.description: Whether to wait for the DOM to settle. Pass false if the script only reads data. Defaults to true.

tools.name: get_console_message
tools.description: Gets a console message by its ID. You can get all messages by calling list_console_messages.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

msgid.description: The msgid of a console message on the page from the listed console messages

tools.name: get_cookies
tools.description: Gets all cookies stored in the browser's default context and writes them, including their values, to a JSON file. The tool reports only which cookies were found (name, domain, and security metadata); cookie values are never returned inline and only exist in the file.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

filePath.description: The absolute or relative path to a .json file to write the cookies (including their values) to.

domain.description: Only return cookies for this domain and its subdomains, e.g. "example.com" also matches "www.example.com" (case-insensitive). When omitted, returns all cookies.

tools.name: get_css_styles
tools.description:
Retrieve matched CSS rules, inline styles (element.style), inherited styles, custom properties, and cascade wrappers (@layer, @media, @container, @scope) for an element identified by its UID.
Rules are ordered from highest to lowest cascade precedence and include source line numbers (e.g. index:196). Active (winning) declarations have no prefix tag, while (losing) overridden declarations are prefixed with [overloaded].
Treat the output as authoritative and complete.
Results are paginated (10 rules per page by default); use pageIdx to page through the remaining rules. Requires a UID from take_snapshot.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

uid.description: The uid of the element on the page from the page content snapshot to inspect CSS styles for

pageSize.description: Maximum number of CSS rules to return per page. Defaults to 10.

pageIdx.description: Page number to return (0-based). Defaults to 0 (the first page).

tools.name: get_network_request
tools.description: Gets a network request by an optional reqid, if omitted returns the currently selected request in the DevTools Network panel. Useful for inspecting request headers (including 'Cookie') and response headers (including 'Set-Cookie' and directives).

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

reqid.description: The reqid of the network request. If omitted returns the currently selected request in the DevTools Network panel.

requestFilePath.description: The absolute or relative path to a .network-request file to save the request body to. If omitted, the body is returned inline.

responseFilePath.description: The absolute or relative path to a .network-response file to save the response body to. If omitted, the body is returned inline.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

tools.description: List all console messages for the target page since the last navigation.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

pageSize.description: Maximum number of messages to return. When omitted, returns all messages.

pageIdx.description: Page number to return (0-based). When omitted, returns the first page.

instructions:
Chrome DevTools MCP lets you drive and inspect live Chrome browser(s) with full DevTools access: navigate, interact with pages, and inspect network, console, performance and memory.

A single Chrome browser is connected. Do not pass a `browserIndex` argument to any tool — every tool automatically targets this browser.

If the connection drops, use `reconnect_browser` to reconnect; the browser must already be running (no start command is configured). Use `list_browsers` to see its connection state and open pages.

Core workflow:
- Call `take_snapshot` to get a structured text snapshot whose elements carry
  `uid`s, then pass those `uid`s to the interaction tools (`click`, `fill`,
  `hover`, `drag`, `fill_form`, ...). Prefer snapshots over screenshots for
  locating elements.
- `list_pages`, `new_page`, `select_page`, `navigate_page` and `wait_for`
  manage tabs and navigation.
- `list_network_requests`, `list_console_messages`, the performance tracing
  tools and the emulation tools support debugging.

Secrets:
- NEVER pass a password or other secret as literal text to `fill`,
  `fill_form`, `type_text`, `set_cookie` or `evaluate_script`: tool
  arguments are recorded in the conversation transcript. Instead stage it
  by reference (e.g.
  `pass show x > ~/.local/share/chrome-devtools-mcp/secrets/<name>`, never `echo "<literal>"`)
  and pass `{{secret:<name>}}`, which this server substitutes just before
  the input reaches the browser, so the value never enters the transcript.
- The secret file is deleted once the call succeeds; append `:keep` to
  retain it, `:raw` to keep a trailing newline. Pick a unique, specific
  name - ~/.local/share/chrome-devtools-mcp/secrets is shared by all MCP servers running in
  parallel.
- A file passed to evaluate_script's `sourcePath` may carry the same
  placeholders; they are resolved after the file is read.
